claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you are looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions about his situation.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or on an approved training course? If so, could you tell me a bit more about what he's studying or the type of course he's on?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment. He left school and isn't doing any courses right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Before I make a final assessment, I just need to check a couple more things:

Is Alex registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for training or work experience? This would apply if he has recently left education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't signed up with anything like that. He just finished school and is taking a bit of time to figure things out, but hasn't registered with careers services or anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me about Alex, I now have enough details to make an assessment.

Let me summarise Alex's situation:
- He is 17 years old
- He is not in full-time education or approved training
- He has not registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation

According to the Child Benefit rules, for children aged 16 or over, you can normally continue to qualify for Child Benefit if the child stays in **approved education or training**. 

Alternatively, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if they register with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service
- The armed services

Since Alex has left school, is not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, I'm afraid you would not currently be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

However, if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England), you could then apply to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks while he is registered. This might be something worth considering.

conversation.text:
I've completed my assessment. To summarise:

**Alex (age 17) - Not Eligible**

Unfortunately, you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because:

1. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if the child remains in approved education or training
2. Alternatively, if a 16 or 17 year old has left education, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
3. Since Alex is not in education/training and hasn't registered with a careers service, the eligibility criteria are not met

**What you could do:**

If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service), you could then apply to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks. This could be helpful while Alex is "figuring things out" and could also provide him with support in exploring his options for work or further training.

If you have any questions about this assessment or Alex's situation changes, please don't hesitate to contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
